The final answer 1164 is correct. I verified it independently.

**Tilings.** A column-by-column transfer analysis over the free-cell sets gives 18 tilings of the 4×6 rectangle. Sixteen have a fault line at the 3|4 boundary, and each half is one of four 4×3 tilings. The other two cross that boundary and have the same column-3 profile.

**Fault-line tilings.** The 4×3 tilings have adjacency graphs K₄−e (two of them, with 6 colorings) or C₄ (two of them, with 18 colorings). Write β = (total colorings)/6, so β = 1 for K₄−e and β = 3 for C₄. Across the fault, only the column-3 pieces (rows 1–2 and rows 3–4) touch the column-4 pieces, giving two cross edges. Counting cross-compatible color assignments gives 18·β_L·β_R per pair. Summing over the 16 pairs:

18 · (1+3+3+1)² = 18 · 64 = 1152.

**Non-fault tilings.** Each of the two has an 8-vertex adjacency graph with 14 edges. Fixing two adjacent triominoes and forcing the rest gives exactly 1 coloring up to the 6 color permutations, so each contributes 6. Total 12.

**Total:** 1152 + 12 = 1164.

VERDICT: ACCEPT
